critique: The black background and turquoise/green palette are appropriate, and the bright centered source reads cleanly. However, the visible result is a compact, opaque concentric bullseye rather than an explosive ring of individually readable particles. It lacks the broad radial spread, broken particulate edge, and energetic outward motion expected from a Ring Explosion thumbnail.

suggestions.why: Expand Direction Spread from the near-zero 2-degree cone into a full radial explosion so particles form a ring rather than a tight central stack.
Increase emitter velocity so the burst reaches a clearly visible ring radius quickly instead of remaining as a small central disk.
Reduce particle size so the expanding ring retains a granular explosive edge instead of merging into a solid turquoise shape.
Reduce the burst density substantially; the current spike overfills the source and hides the separate exploding particles.
